summary: Both sides are the same static single-colour exponential spot with an identical control surface, and every explicitly-dialed setting of all three controls matches to within 0-2 of 255; the only real gaps are the untouched defaults (port's spot is ~1.7x wider, hue 0.78 vs 0.77) and a slightly steeper falloff at sharpness <= 0.1 where the original goes perfectly flat and the port does not.
observations: STATIC FIELD on both sides: baseline (6 s / 20 fps), survey (60 s / 5 fps) and a late window (--skip 20 --seconds 30 --fps 4) all post motion 0 / motionLit 0, zeroMotionFrames = every captured frame, brightnessTrend 'steady', and min==max on every stats series. Dumps at t=0, 3 and 5.5 s are byte-identical per side. There is no animation, no mode rotation and no drift to compare, so the temporal machinery is a no-op; judging pivoted to dial and rig sweeps.
Seed independence confirmed: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce byte-identical frames on BOTH sides (compared per-pixel, not by stats).

Control surface is IDENTICAL: both sides expose hsvPickerColor (hsvPicker, label 'Color'), sliderSharpness (slider, 'Sharpness'), sliderLocation (slider, 'Location'). No compile or runtime errors on either side. wantsSensors false on both.

Shape family matches exactly: a single symmetric exponential-decay bump on the flat pixel index, peak at the location pixel, decaying by a constant ratio per pixel outward. Log-linear fits of the falloff constant k (per pixel) at matched dial settings: sharpness 0.25 -> orig 0.1402 / port 0.1418; 0.5 -> 0.4550 / 0.4545; 0.75 -> 0.9755 / 0.9730; 1.0 -> 1.7707 / 1.7707. k tracks ~1.7 * sharpness^2 on both sides.

DIALED sharpness sweep (hsvPickerColor=0.33,1,1; sliderLocation=0.5; 60 px strip), max abs per-channel difference orig vs port: s=1.0 -> 0 (byte-identical), s=0.75 -> 1, s=0.5 -> 1, s=0.4 -> 1, s=0.35 -> 1, s=0.30 -> 1, s=0.275 -> 2, s=0.25 -> 2, s=0.225 -> 2, s=0.20 -> 3, s=0.175 -> 3, s=0.15 -> 4, s=0.125 -> 6, s=0.10 -> 9, s=0.08 -> 11, s=0.05 -> 14, s=0.02 -> 17, s=0.01 -> 17, s=0 -> 18. FWHM in pixels is identical between sides at every value from 0.15 up (31, 25/23, 19, 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5 px).

SHARPNESS=0 EDGE CASE is the one structural difference: the original renders a perfectly FLAT full-brightness strip (all 60 px at 255 on the driven channel), while the port renders a shallow bump, 237 at the ends rising to 255 at centre - a 7% dimming at the strip ends that the original does not have. Equivalent to the port's sharpness->decay mapping carrying a small additive offset (k ~ 0.0026/px at s=0 instead of 0). The gap decays monotonically with sharpness and is under 1% by s=0.25.

DIALED location sweep (sharpness 0.5) matches essentially exactly: loc=0 peaks at px 0, 0.25 at px 15, 0.5 at px 30, 0.75 at px 45, loc=1 puts the peak at px 60 (just off the end, leaving a rising ramp ending at 167). Max abs difference 1 count at every setting, from a single rounding disagreement (orig 109 vs port 108).

DIALED hsvPicker sweep matches exactly. Hue at s=1,v=1: h=0 -> both (255,0,0); 0.17 -> both (249,255,0); 0.33 -> both (5,255,0); 0.5 -> both (0,255,255); 0.67 -> both (5,0,255); 0.83 -> both (249,0,255); 1 -> both (255,0,0). Saturation x value grid (h=0.6; s in 0/0.5/1, v in 0.25/0.6/1) is byte-identical in 6 of 9 cells and off by at most 1 count in the rest, e.g. s=1,v=0.25 -> both (0,25,63); s=0.5,v=1 -> both (127,178,255).

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIVERGE (both sides render, neither is degenerate, but they are visibly different). Original: violet peak (158,0,255) = hue 0.770, FWHM 15 px of 60, strip ends at (4,0,7). Port: violet peak (173,0,255) = hue ~0.780, FWHM 25 px of 60, strip ends at (21,0,31). Mean brightness 45 (orig) vs 67 (port). Cross-dialing pins it: the ORIGINAL driven at hsvPickerColor=0.78,1,1 / sliderSharpness=0.17 reproduces the PORT's untouched render to max 4 counts (mean 1.58), while the original driven at 0.77,1,1 / sliderSharpness=0.225 reproduces its OWN untouched render to max 1 count. So the port's built-in default sharpness is ~0.17 against the original's ~0.225 (a ~1.7x wider spot) and its default hue is ~0.78 against 0.77.

Both sides are INDEX-ONLY, identically so: on a 16x16 grid (--rig grid --grid 16x16, sharpness 0.5, location 0.5) neither draws a 2D blob - both draw a band running along the serpentine flat index, peaking mid-row-8 and decaying along the index in both directions, matching each other to max 1 count.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way: the spot width is a fixed FRACTION of the strip, not a fixed pixel count. At sharpness 0.5 / location 0.5, FWHM is 1 px at 12 px, 7 px at 60 px (13 px), 7 px at 120 px and 17 px at 300 px - identical on both sides at every rig size (max abs diff 0 at 12 px, 1 at 120 and 300 px).

dials.name: hsvPickerColor
dials.origEffect: hsvPicker; sets the spot's colour directly. Sweeping hue 0->1 walks red->yellow->green->cyan->blue->magenta->red; saturation desaturates toward white; value scales overall brightness linearly (v=0.25 peak (0,25,63) at h=0.6,s=1). Probe maxDelta 44.87.
dials.portEffect: Identical across the whole HSV space tested (7 hues x full range, plus a 3x3 saturation/value grid): byte-identical in most cells, max 1 count elsewhere. Probe maxDelta 66.59 (larger only because the port's untouched baseline it is compared against is brighter).

dials.name: sliderSharpness
dials.origEffect: Controls the exponential falloff rate, k ~ 1.7*s^2 per pixel: s=0 gives a perfectly flat full-brightness strip, s=0.15 FWHM 31 px, s=0.25 FWHM 13 px, s=0.5 FWHM ~5 px, s=1 a near-single-pixel spot (255,47,8,1 tail). Monotone, continuous, no mode boundaries. Probe maxDelta 92.80.
dials.portEffect: Same law and same FWHM at every value from 0.15 to 1.0 (max abs diff 1-4 counts). Diverges only at the very low end, where the port never fully flattens: at s=0 the port's ends sit at 237/255 vs the original's 255 (max diff 18), at s=0.05 max diff 14, at s=0.08 max diff 11. Probe maxDelta 71.57.

dials.name: sliderLocation
dials.origEffect: Linearly positions the spot's peak along the strip: 0 -> pixel 0, 0.25 -> pixel 15, 0.5 -> pixel 30, 0.75 -> pixel 45, 1 -> pixel 60 (off the end, leaving only the rising half). No wrap-around - the off-strip half is simply clipped. Probe maxDelta 53.61.
dials.portEffect: Identical peak pixel at every value, identical clipping behaviour at loc=0 and loc=1, max abs difference 1 count throughout. Probe maxDelta 62.76.

feedback: Untouched default sharpness is too low in the port. The port's built-in default renders a spot of FWHM 25 px on a 60 px strip with the ends at 12% brightness (21,0,31); the original renders FWHM 15 px with the ends at 3% (4,0,7). Cross-dialing shows the port's default is equivalent to sliderSharpness ~0.17 while the original's is ~0.225. Raise the port's initial sharpness value so an untouched load produces the narrower spot. This is the only difference a viewer would notice on load (mean brightness 45 vs 67).

Untouched default hue is off by ~0.01. Original's untouched peak is (158,0,255) = hue 0.770; the port's is (173,0,255) = hue ~0.780. Set the port's initial picker hue to 0.77 exactly. Cosmetically negligible but trivially fixable, and it is the only reason the untouched renders are not reproducible from the same dial values.

At sharpness = 0 the original produces a perfectly uniform full-brightness strip (all 60 px at 255); the port produces a shallow bump that dims to 237/255 (-7%) at the strip ends. The port's falloff appears to carry a small additive term (~0.0026 per pixel of decay) that the original does not, so it never reaches a true flat wash. The residue scales down with sharpness (max diff 18 at s=0, 14 at s=0.05, 11 at s=0.08, 4 at s=0.15, 2 at s=0.225, <=1 above s=0.3), so only the bottom ~15% of the slider is affected. Make s=0 collapse the exponent exactly to zero.

Nothing else needs touching: at every explicitly-dialed setting of all three controls the two renders agree to 0-2 of 255, including full-range hue/saturation/value sweeps, the location slider's endpoints and off-strip clipping, index-only pixel mapping on a 16x16 grid, and resolution scaling at 12/60/120/300 px. Do not 'fix' the shape, the colour conversion, or the location mapping.
